claim_scope: Research-only bounded replay evidence for ZenoDEX tau-value table semantics on the exact locked IDNI/tau-lang revision. Rows are tau fact values, tables are joins of rows, SELECT/foreign-key lookup is meet, append-only growth is join, and a temporal asset-registry gate admits a transfer contribution only when its asset key exists in the previous registry state. An absent key annihilates the contribution to 0, making ledger append an exact no-op. This packet supersedes the earlier v4 nonclaim that table semantics were not exercised; it does not claim a separate SQL-style Table type or keyword.
failure_modes: an absent asset key still contributes a transfer row to the ledger
an annihilated transfer contribution changes the prior transfer table
append-only join removes rows already represented by the prior table
independent row inserts produce order-dependent table values
an exact duplicate row changes the table value
a same-step asset registration is allowed to vouch for its own transfer despite the previous-state gate
the table replay runs against a mutable Tau branch name instead of the exact locked source revision
the bounded table model is overstated as production storage, authorization, replay protection, or settlement authority

aaa.reason: The replay arranges fixed existing/missing asset keys, exact duplicate rows and same-step/prior-step boundary cases, acts through Tau's own theorem queries plus the temporal run, and asserts the complete expected T/F sequence and execution of the structured table stream on the exact locked source.

reject_is_noop.reason: The table contract proves that an invalid transfer contribution annihilated to 0 leaves the transfer table unchanged under join, directly mirroring ZenoDEX reject-as-noop discipline at the bounded logical-table layer.

boundary_dimensions.name: asset_registry_membership
points: asset id 1 overlaps a registry containing ids 1 and 2
asset id 7 has no overlap with that registry

boundary_dimensions.name: foreign_key_transfer_gate
points: a transfer whose asset id exists in the registry survives the meet unchanged
a transfer whose asset id is absent is annihilated to 0

boundary_dimensions.name: temporal_activation
points: a newly inserted asset cannot self-authorize a transfer in the same step because the gate reads assets[t-1]
the same asset key can authorize a later-step transfer once it exists in the previous registry

boundary_dimensions.name: table_growth_algebra
points: exact duplicate row append is idempotent
appending an invalid zero contribution is an exact no-op

nonclaims: This evidence grants no production, settlement, publication, verifier, migration, release, or value-moving authority.
The table is a tau-value logical row set, not a claim about a SQL engine, physical storage layout, indexing, query planning, dynamic COUNT, or unbounded row iteration.
Asset ids, transaction ids, identities and amounts are bounded abstract tags; no production u128/u256 arithmetic is modeled.

The asset-registry gate proves only key existence in the bounded logical table; it does not prove asset enabled status, authorization, sender balance, fee validity, signatures, canonical encoding, hashing, proof verification, or policy membership.
Exact duplicate row idempotence is not a proof of transaction-id uniqueness: a row reusing the same tx_id with different other members requires a separate replay/nonce index contract.
The temporal contract intentionally imposes prior-state activation: an asset inserted at step t cannot authorize a transfer until a later step.
This evidence does not close O-008 or any whole-value-movement gate and does not make the pre-existing P22 formal-cycle packet current.
The third-party tutorial motivated the table model, but the admitted claim depends only on the ZenoDEX spec replayed against the exact locked Tau source.
